title: HE WORSHIPPED AS HE LEANED ON HIS STAFF

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Swear to me,' he said. Then Joseph swore to him, and Israel worshipped as he leaned on the top of his staff." — Gen 47:31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a picture to end the chapter with. An old man, too weak to stand unsupported, leaning on his staff — and worshipping.

Hebrews singles out this exact moment as an act of faith: "By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons, and worshipped as he leaned on the top of his staff" (Heb 11:21). Of everything in Jacob's long and complicated life, this is the scene the New Testament chose to remember.

Not his cleverness. Not his wrestling at Peniel. His worship at the end, with a staff under his hand.

There is real comfort here for anyone whose strength is failing — through age, illness, or exhaustion. Worship does not require strength. It requires a heart turned towards God. Jacob could not stand on his own, so he leaned, and he worshipped anyway.

And think about what that staff represented. It had carried him across the Jordan as a frightened young man running from his brother with nothing (Gen 32:10). It had walked with him through every hard year since. Now, at the end, he leans on it and worships the God who brought him all that way.

Whatever you are leaning on today, let it hold you up while you worship.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is God worthy of your worship for today, regardless of how you feel?
2. Have you believed worship requires strength or a good day?
3. Looking back, what has God carried you through?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when my strength fails, let my heart still turn to You. Thank You for carrying me this far. I worship You today, leaning on Your faithfulness. Amen.
